children: Australian stocks could look set to wrap up what would be their worst week in at least 17 months, with local futures pointing to another opening fall. The S&P/ASX 200 is on a five-day losing streak and is already down by 3.9% so far this week. With ASX futures down by 1.1% ahead of Friday's session, the benchmark index is likely to beat the 3.9% drop it recorded in early April 2025. It hasn't lost more than that since June 2022 and could even record its largest weekly decline since March 2020, when Covid-19 was roiling global markets. Ahead of the open, data-center operator NextDC said it paused some developments and tightened spending rules following costly delays at one of its Melbourne sites. All three major U.S. indices lost between 2.0% and 2.25%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
